hf_evidence_type: transcript + protein (plasma) + clinical; myocardial and atrial expression and plasma ANP rise with wall stress in human HF; guideline biomarker
receptor_cancer_evidence: Mixed and contradictory. NPR1 is pro-tumorigenic in gastric cancer (knockdown causes G2/M arrest; anti-NPR1 antibody reduces xenograft burden; PMID 27634171, 38151776), yet ANP-family peptides are reported to kill cancer cells in vitro at micromolar doses (PMID 16297362). No functional evidence for NPR3 in solid tumours retrieved.
notes: BNP had no antiproliferative effect even at 100x the active ANP concentration (16297362), so the two natriuretic peptides are not interchangeable. Anticancer claims come largely from one research programme at supraphysiological doses.

hf_evidence_type: transcript + protein (plasma) + clinical; the diagnostic HF biomarker; circulating form is predominantly weakly-active proBNP
receptor_cancer_evidence: Weak. No retrieved study shows BNP or proBNP driving solid tumour growth through NPR1; the one direct in vitro comparison found BNP inactive against cancer cells (16297362).
notes: Transcript elevation in myocardium is unambiguous, but the dominant circulating species is proBNP with low receptor activity - a transcript-level nomination overstates the bioactive signal.

hf_evidence_type: receptor, not an HF-secreted ligand
receptor_cancer_evidence: Pro-tumorigenic in gastric cancer with antibody proof-of-concept in xenografts (38151776) and ROS/cell-cycle mechanism (27634171); high tumour NPR1 predicted recurrence.
notes: Evidence concentrated in gastric cancer; not generalised across tumour types.

hf_evidence_type: receptor for CNP, not an HF ligand
receptor_cancer_evidence: No direct solid-tumour functional evidence retrieved.
notes: Marked unsupported for cancer relevance.

hf_evidence_type: clearance receptor
receptor_cancer_evidence: No solid-tumour evidence retrieved.
notes: Any nomination of NPR3 as a tumour receptor axis would be unsupported by retrieved literature.

hf_evidence_type: protein (plasma) + clinical; plasma proenkephalin A elevated in acute HF and HFpEF and independently prognostic
receptor_cancer_evidence: Classical receptors: contradictory. OPRK1 and OPRD1 transcripts are enriched in tumours pan-cancer but with no survival association after adjustment (35359418); nuclear KOR predicted poor prognosis in oesophageal SCC (23574786) while KOR agonism was anti-angiogenic and KOR-knockout tumours grew faster (24225480). The met-enkephalin growth effect that IS reproducible runs through OGFR, a nuclear-envelope protein unrelated to the GPCRs (11890982, 21531450).
notes: Critical caveat: PENK elevation in HF is driven mainly by renal function - eGFR was the strongest independent predictor and PENK clustered with renal markers (31091993). Elevated plasma PENK in HF is substantially a cardiorenal readout, not proof of cardiac secretion.

hf_evidence_type: not an HF ligand
receptor_cancer_evidence: Transcript higher in tumour than normal tissue pan-cancer (OR 1.27) but NOT associated with disease-free interval or overall survival after adjustment (35359418). Nuclear KOR prognostic in oesophageal SCC (23574786). KOR agonists suppressed tumour angiogenesis via VEGFR2 and KOR-knockout mice grew larger tumours (24225480) - i.e. the direction of effect is anti-tumour.
notes: The single most important counter-finding for an OPRK1 axis: higher tumour expression does not translate into worse outcome, and pharmacology points the opposite way.

hf_evidence_type: not an HF ligand
receptor_cancer_evidence: Highest tumour-versus-normal transcript enrichment of the three classical receptors (OR 1.66) but again no adjusted outcome association (35359418).
notes: The two hepatocellular-carcinoma papers most often cited for DOR-driven progression are RETRACTED (PMIDs 23903826, 26549838) and were excluded here.

hf_evidence_type: not an HF ligand
receptor_cancer_evidence: The best-studied receptor: protein overexpressed in lung cancer and higher in metastatic cases (24920011), MOR expression plus opioid requirement predicted worse survival in prostate cancer (24104703). But transcript is LOWER in tumour than normal tissue pan-cancer (OR 0.74; 35359418), and two randomised trials found opioid-sparing anaesthesia did not reduce recurrence (31645288, 34192298).
notes: Direction of transcript change is opposite to the protein/IHC literature - a caution for any transcript-only nomination.

hf_evidence_type: transcript + protein (myocardium); periostin mRNA up and protein detectable only in failing hearts, correlating with fibrosis; localised to a FAP/POSTN disease-associated fibroblast state in human HF
receptor_cancer_evidence: Strong and consistent. Periostin drives ovarian cancer migration, invasion and metastasis via integrin beta-3/beta-5-ERK-NF-kB (36550569) and periostin-high CAFs promote lymph node metastasis in cervical SCC by breaking lymphatic endothelial barriers (33124726).
notes: The best-supported axis in this list, and the only ligand identified from an unbiased HF-serum depletion experiment (32475164). But Postn-knockout mice still showed cardiac-remodelling-dependent tumour promotion (38139195), so periostin is sufficient but not necessary.

hf_evidence_type: transcript/protein in cardiac disease reported at family level only; SFRP1-specific human HF evidence not retrieved
receptor_cancer_evidence: Tumour-suppressive: SFRP1 is silenced by promoter hypermethylation in most breast cancers and SFRP overexpression inhibits growth (18283316, 24316024).
notes: Direction problem: SFRPs are Wnt ANTAGONISTS. More SFRP ligand predicts LESS Wnt-driven tumour growth, so a positive ligand-receptor compatibility score would have the wrong sign.

hf_evidence_type: protein (animal myocardium) + functional; upregulated after MI in rat and in the failing hamster heart, antibody blockade improved ejection fraction; human HF plasma evidence not retrieved
receptor(s): FZD receptors; also inhibits BMP1 procollagen processing
receptor_cancer_evidence: Tumour-suppressive by family-level evidence (24316024); SFRP2 is methylated in 100% of tested breast cancer cell lines (18283316).
notes: Human HF evidence is limited to animal and hamster models; effect is on fibrosis, and cancer direction is antagonistic.

hf_evidence_type: not an HF ligand
receptor_cancer_evidence: Strong in cancer generally: FZD2 drives EMT and metastasis via a noncanonical Fyn-STAT3 pathway and an anti-FZD2 antibody inhibits xenograft growth (25417160); high FZD2 predicts poor prognosis in HCC (30677195) and breast cancer (33832493); pan-cancer upregulation (40444048). For GYNAECOLOGIC cancer specifically the evidence is INDIRECT: WNT5A is upregulated across all major ovarian subtypes (24924122), host-derived WNT5A drives peritoneal metastasis (31932454), and WNT5A overexpression upregulates FZD2/FZD5 in ovarian lines (33723319) - but no study retrieved measures FZD2 in ovarian or endometrial tumours as a primary endpoint.
notes: This is a genuine gap: targeted searches for FZD2 in ovarian/endometrial cancer returned no direct study. If the analysis nominates a FZD2-gynaecologic axis, the paper must state that FZD2 itself is unvalidated in these tumours and that the supporting evidence is the WNT5A-FZD2/FZD5 relationship.

hf_evidence_type: protein (plasma) + clinical; elevated in HFpEF and HFrEF, independently prognostic, marks inflammatory pathway activation
receptor_cancer_evidence: GFRAL is restricted to the area postrema and nucleus tractus solitarius of the brainstem (28953886), so circulating GDF15 cannot signal to peripheral tumour cells through its canonical receptor. The established cancer role is host cachexia: anti-GFRAL antibody reverses cachexia in tumour-bearing mice (32661391).
notes: Decisive receptor-compatibility failure. GDF15 is one of the best-established HF-elevated ligands but its receptor is not expressed on tumours - a useful NEGATIVE CONTROL for a compatibility-scoring design. Note GDF15 also predicts incident cancer in the community (28062617), which is confounding, not signalling.

hf_evidence_type: transcript (myocardium); recurrent across failing-myocardium microarray meta-analysis and nominated as an HF-secreted candidate in the founding HF-tumour experiment
receptor(s): No defined single-pass receptor; acts as a protease inhibitor / nuclear-binding secretory serpin
receptor_cancer_evidence: Bidirectional by tumour type: tumour-suppressive in lung cancer (37417362) but tumour-promoting in triple-negative breast cancer (33569740); reviews conclude compartment- and cancer-specific function with obscure mechanism (35843512).
notes: SERPINA3 has no canonical receptor, so it cannot be scored in a ligand-receptor compatibility framework at all. Human HF plasma quantification was not retrieved. Its prominence rests on being a candidate in Meijers 2018, not on independent validation.

hf_evidence_type: transcript + protein (plasma) + human clinical; plasma CTGF correlates with E/e' and MRI fibrosis in diastolic HF, tissue CTGF rises with stretch and in canine aortic banding
receptor(s): Integrins (ITGAV/ITGB3, ITGB5); LRP; heparan sulfate proteoglycans
receptor_cancer_evidence: Contradictory by tumour type: hepatoma CTGF drives integrin/NF-kB-IL-6-STAT3 crosstalk promoting HCC (36210625), but CTGF overexpression REDUCED lung adenocarcinoma invasion and metastasis via integrin alphav-beta3/beta5-CRMP1 (14996858).
notes: Serious paracrine caveat: cell-specific knockout showed cardiomyocyte-derived CCN2 is dispensable and CCN2 acts AUTOCRINE on fibroblasts (30040954). Cardiac CCN2 transcript elevation therefore poorly supports an endocrine tumour-promoting signal.

hf_evidence_type: transcript + protein (myocardium and serum) + clinical; serum 56% above matched controls in systolic HF, myocardial protein 2.5-fold higher in explanted failing hearts, also raised in HFpEF
receptor(s): DIP2A; TLR4; also binds BMP4/DIP2A-independent routes
receptor_cancer_evidence: Pro-tumorigenic with a defined receptor: fibroblast-secreted FSTL1 promotes HCC growth, metastasis and stemness via TLR4-AKT/mTOR (34551961), and DIP2A expression on tumour cells is required for FSTL1-driven immunoresistance with FSTL1/DIP2A co-positivity predicting poor NSCLC prognosis (30110636).
notes: Direction conflict within the heart: cardiomyocyte Fstl1 deletion WORSENED HFpEF (27430031), so cardiac FSTL1 is protective locally while the same protein is pro-tumorigenic peripherally. Elevated FSTL1 in HF may be a compensatory response.

hf_evidence_type: transcript + protein (animal and human myocardium); expression increases markedly in hypertrophic and failing hearts, knockout worsens post-TAC fibrosis
receptor(s): Integrin alpha-2 (ITGA2); also intracellular ER-stress role
receptor_cancer_evidence: Pro-tumorigenic with a defined receptor: CAF-derived TSP-4 binds integrin alpha-2 on gallbladder cancer cells to phosphorylate HSF1 and drive proliferation and stem-like traits (33407730); THBS4 is induced in breast cancer-associated stroma (23942617).
notes: THBS4 in cancer is a STROMAL response protein, not a tumour-cell product - so its tumour relevance is already about locally produced ligand, which weakens the case that a distant cardiac source adds signal. THBS4 also has an intracellular ER function, so transcript up does not mean secretion up.

hf_evidence_type: direction is OPPOSITE: COMP expression was DECREASED in dilated cardiomyopathy patient hearts versus donors, and COMP-knockout mice spontaneously developed DCM
receptor_cancer_evidence: Overexpressed in 15 human cancers pan-cancer with diagnostic ROC value and immune-evasion association (36255654).
notes: Should NOT be listed as an HF-upregulated ligand. If a transcript analysis nominates COMP as up in HF, that contradicts the published human myocardial direction and needs explicit comment.

hf_evidence_type: protein (plasma) + clinical + meta-analysis; each 1 SD plasma galectin-3 associated with all-cause mortality HR 1.10, CVD mortality HR 1.22, incident HF HR 1.12
receptor(s): No single canonical receptor; binds glycans on integrins, CD146/MCAM, CD47, EGFR and others
receptor_cancer_evidence: Broadly pro-tumorigenic through glycan-dependent interactions with multiple surface partners rather than one receptor.
notes: Decisive caveat for a transcript-based design: plasma galectin-3 did NOT correlate with myocardial galectin-3 or with LV fibrosis in endomyocardial biopsies (28288987). Cardiac transcript, cardiac protein and plasma level are dissociated. Also no single receptor gene to score.

hf_evidence_type: protein (plasma) + clinical; serially measured IGFBP-7 levels and slopes independently predicted outcome after adjustment for NT-proBNP and troponin
receptor(s): IGF1R (indirect, via IGF sequestration); insulin receptor
receptor_cancer_evidence: Direction is tumour-type dependent: IGFBP7 overexpression predicted worse survival in gastric cancer (26043748) but expression was LOWER than normal epithelium with LOH and promoter methylation in high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma (25886299).
notes: IGFBP7 modulates IGF availability rather than binding a dedicated receptor, so 'ligand-receptor compatibility' is a poor model for its action.

hf_evidence_type: protein (myocardium); endomyocardial CXCL12/SDF-1 positive in 65.4% of inflammatory versus 19.1% of non-inflammatory cardiomyopathy biopsies and predicted mortality; general chemokine upregulation in injured myocardium is established
receptor_cancer_evidence: Strong and canonical: the CXCL12-CXCR4/CXCR7 axis drives tumour proliferation, angiogenesis and metastasis across many cancers (37497001).
notes: Human HF (as opposed to inflammatory cardiomyopathy) plasma CXCL12 elevation was not established by retrieved evidence. Chemokines are produced by essentially every inflamed tissue, so cardiac origin cannot be inferred from a plasma or transcript signal.

hf_evidence_type: protein (plasma) + transcript (myocardium) in a mouse post-MI HF model; human HF evidence not retrieved
receptor_cancer_evidence: Circulating NGF elevated after MI drove mammary tumour growth via TRKA-PI3K-AKT, and TRKA inhibition suppressed tumour volume in vivo (38510296).
notes: Included because it is the only HF-secreted ligand with a complete ligand-receptor-inhibitor causal chain in vivo, but the evidence is entirely murine - no human HF plasma NGF data retrieved.
